summary: Redwood AE + SE walked NewTerra through the Console usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdown. Customer is interested in reducing token cost for high-volume routes, wants visibility per route and SLO tagging. Action: share pricing, security docs, and schedule POC benchmarks.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we're Jordan from Redwood, and with me is Priya, our solutions engineer. Thanks for taking time.
[00:06] Mark Holloway: Hey Jordan, thanks. Quick note, we have Diego on for FinOps questions, Sara's on for infra.
[00:12] Speaker 1: Great, should I kick off with a share?
[00:16] Jordan Kim: Yep, I'm going to share the Console — link posted in the chat: https://redwood.ai/console-demo (note: demo link, not prod).
[00:24] Priya Shah: Cool, so high-level agenda: we will go through usage analytics, per-route dashboards, cost breakdown per model/route, then recommendations like batching and KV caching and finally next steps for a POC.
[00:36] [00:40] Mark: Sounds good. Our main ask is: we have a multi-tenant financial assistant, high qps on short prompts for triage, and a few long-form summarization routes. We want to see per-route cost and latency so FinOps can optimize.
[00:52] Jordan Kim: Totally, that's what the per-route dashboards were built for. Priya, can you open the Usage page?
[00:56] Priya Shah: Yep opening — okay here is the top-level usage analytics. You can see tokens over time, error rate, p95 latency, and cost estimate by day. Quick caveat — cost numbers here are modeled on your selected instance/plan and can be tuned.
[01:12] Sara Reyes: I see a filter for routes, and for model version. Is that per-env too? prod/stage?
[01:18] Priya Shah: Yes, you can filter by environment, customer segment, route name, model family, and also tag by SLO. The tags are freeform so you can do things like "high-priority" or "sensitive-data".
[01:28] [01:30] Diego Torres: How does Redwood compute the cost breakdown? Is it per-token only or do you include infra and reserved capacity amortization?
[01:36] Jordan Kim: Good question. The Console shows an estimated unit cost per token using our hosted rates as baseline; for Dedicated we let you input committed capacity and we amortize reserved GPU cost across tokens in the selected timeframe. So you'll see a split: model cost (per-token), infra amortized, and overhead (network, caching).
[01:52] Priya Shah: I'm going to open an example route, "triage-short" — you can see calls, avg tokens in/out, and a cost per call number. Notice on the right we show model selection history — when you switched from gpt-large-open to rw-optimized-1.2 it cut token cost by about 18% but p95 latency changed slightly.
[02:12] Mark Holloway: That model name is a little different in our docs, is rw-optimized the Redwood verified opt?
[02:16] Priya Shah: Yes that's our optimized family — sometimes the transcript picks that up oddly, you might see it as "redwood op'" in the export.
[02:22] [02:24] Speaker 2: There's a graph that shows cost per route over time, with annotations for deploys, can we export that?
[02:29] Priya Shah: Yes export csv or png. Also we have a cost-trend API if you prefer programmatic pulls for FinOps dashboards.
[02:36] Diego Torres: For the amortized reserved capacity example, can you show how a burst policy factors in? We plan to reserve baseline but need bursts during earnings days.
[02:44] Jordan Kim: Sure — on the right you can configure reserved commit and burst. The forecast calculator simulates your traffic and shows expected unit cost with and without burst. It will also show risk of fallback to hosted variants if dedicated capacity is saturated.
[02:58] [03:00] Sara Reyes: How accurate are the forecasts? We push sudden spikes occasionally, and we've had caches warm vs cold issues.
[03:06] Priya Shah: Forecasts are as-good-as your input traffic profile. For caches we add a separate "cache hit" slider — if your KV cache hit rate is high, effective token cost drops significantly. Also we can simulate cold start latencies; our runtime preserves KV cache between requests for the same session if you use session affinity. Sometimes the transcript exports that as "K V cash" or similar.
[03:26] Mark Holloway: Any way to break down cost by customer segment within a single route? We route multiple tenants to same function.
[03:32] Priya Shah: Yep you can pass a route header or tenant tag and the Console will attribute usage by tenant. We show per-tenant cost so you can decide to shard heavy tenants onto separate pools.
[03:42] [03:45] Jordan Kim: Let's jump to a per-route dashboard example where we show p50/p95, tokens, cost per call, and top prompts. Priya click "triage-short" then "top prompts".
[03:53] Priya Shah: Here — top prompts is from our eval logs, we redact PII but you can view anonymized clusters. This helps you find prompt patterns causing long context lengths.
[04:05] Diego Torres: Do you support synthetic replay for bench? e.g., replay last 24h traffic to a dedicated pool for a dry run?
[04:10] Priya Shah: Yes, we have a replay tool — it's in beta in Console (link in notes) that will spin up a test pool and replay traffic with matching timing. Useful for cost and latency verification.
[04:20] [04:24] Mark Holloway: Ok can we talk about batching — we saw Redwood's docs mention continuous batching and it sounded like it might affect latency predictability.
[04:30] Priya Shah: Good call. Our runtime does continuous batching with per-route controls. For low-latency routes you can set max wait and max batch size. The Console will simulate latency vs cost tradeoff if you toggle those knobs. For example, increasing max wait to 10ms might reduce cost by X% at negligible p95 impact for short prompts.
[04:52] Speaker 1: I noticed a "quantization profile" in the console — does that change output quality?
[04:56] Priya Shah: It's a lever — we recommend certain profiles per model family and workload. The Console shows quality/regression monitors tied to evals so you can see if a quantization switch caused any eval regression.
[05:08] [05:12] Diego Torres: Security/regulatory question — we process sensitive ledger mentions. How do audit logs and encryption show up in Console?
[05:18] Jordan Kim: We have audit trails for API calls, model versions, and admin actions. For Private deployments you can integrate KMS/HSM; for Dedicated we also support customer-managed keys via cloud KMS. We'll share SOC 2 + architecture doc after the call.
[05:30] Sara Reyes: Are there RBAC roles scoped to routes and to cost centers? We have strict separation.
[05:34] Priya Shah: Yes RBAC can be scoped to route groups and data environments; and you can export cost attribution per cost-center.
[05:42] [05:45] Mark Holloway: Let's go through an example cost breakdown for a high-volume route. Diego — I'll pass you over to you for the sample numbers.
[05:51] Diego Torres: Sure, baseline: 2M calls / month, avg tokens in 20, tokens out 60, target p95 < 300ms, sensitive false. What would our cost look like hosted vs dedicated?
[06:02] Priya Shah: Inputting those numbers into the forecast — hosted estimated unit cost ~ $0.0032 per call (modeled), total ~ $6.4k/month. Dedicated with a small reserved pool (1xA10 equivalent) amortized gives ~ $3.6k/month but with a burst add-on of +20% when needed. Those are ballpark — we'll send a tailored sheet.
[06:22] Jordan Kim: Important nuance: the per-call estimate assumes prefix caching disabled; if you enable prefix/KV caching and 60% hit rate we show effective cost per call drop to ~$1.8k/month.
[06:34] [06:36] Mark Holloway: That's a big delta. How easy is it to implement the KV cache?
[06:40] Priya Shah: It's a few lines in the SDK to set session keys; for server-side you can use our caching middleware. We'll include sample code snippets in the follow-up.
[06:50] Speaker 3: What about model fallback: if dedicated capacity is saturated and latency spikes, do requests fail?
[06:56] Jordan Kim: We recommend automatic fallback policies: route-level policy can fallback to a compatible hosted variant with slightly higher cost but preserves availability. Console will show expected fallback rate under simulated traffic.
[07:08] [07:12] Sara Reyes: Is there auditability on rollouts? We need to show who promoted a model and when in our internal reviews.
[07:18] Priya Shah: Yes rollout history, who initiated canary and percentage, and performance changes are recorded; you can tie that into alerts.
[07:26] Mark Holloway: OK — a few nitty-gritty items for POC: 1) we'll need SOC 2 and network diagrams, 2) a list of supported KMS providers, 3) a replay test with our last 48h traffic, 4) sample pricing for 6/12 month reserved.
[07:44] Jordan Kim: Great — those are exactly the items we'll deliver. I'll take pricing and SOC2, Priya will take benchmarks and replay config.
[07:52] [07:56] Diego Torres: One more — can the Console show per-route SLO alerts and hook into our PagerDuty? We want to be alerted on cost anomalies too.
[08:02] Priya Shah: Yes SLO alerting and cost anomaly detection exist; we can integrate with PagerDuty, Slack, or webhook. You can set thresholds on cost-per-route or percent-change.
[08:14] Speaker 1: We've hit about 8 minutes of Q&A — any other deep dives?
[08:18] Jordan Kim: Maybe a quick look at the API export: you can pull per-route metrics via our metrics API, e.g., /v1/metrics/routes?start=... We'll drop example curl in the follow-up.
[08:30] Priya Shah: Also note we support programmatic tagging; once you tag requests with "customer_id" the Console attribution is automatic.
[08:38] [08:40] Mark Holloway: Timing — we're leaning toward a Dedicated POC with a 4-week benchmark. We're concerned about initial integration time and who from Redwood will help onboard.
[08:50] Jordan Kim: We'll assign a Solutions Architect during the POC and include runbooks. Typical onboarding is 1-2 weeks for the basic integration and then benchmarking.
[08:58] Diego Torres: For the POC, please include a cost model comparing current provider (we'll send our current invoice) vs Redwood dedicated.
[09:04] Priya Shah: Noted. We'll template the cost model and you can drop your numbers.
[09:10] [09:12] Speaker 2: There's some transcription mismatch here but looks good.
[09:16] Jordan Kim: Cool, recap of next steps: Jordan send pricing & SOC2, Priya send benchmarks & replay guide, Mark to share traffic profile and current invoice, schedule POC start Nov 20th.
[09:28] Mark Holloway: Confirmed. Thanks everyone.
[09:32] Sara Reyes: Thanks, bye.
[09:34] [end transcript]
